title: What is Flink's failover strategy: region failover (only restart the failed region/pipeline, not the entire job graph) vs full restart: and why is region failover the default and more efficient?
keyPoints: The failover strategy decides how much of the job graph to restart, while the restart strategy decides how often.
Region failover restarts only the failed pipelined region and its dependents, leaving unrelated regions running.
A pipelined region is a set of tasks connected by streaming data exchanges, bounded by blocking exchanges.
Region failover has been the default since Flink 1.9 because it minimizes the blast radius of a single failure.
Full restart cancels every task in the entire job, which is simple but wasteful for multi-pipeline jobs.
Batch and hybrid jobs benefit most from region failover because blocking exchanges create smaller regions.
Region failover depends on checkpointing so the restarted region can restore state consistently.

s1_definition.oneliner: Region failover restarts only the failed pipelined region and its dependents, not the whole job, which is why it is the default and more efficient than full restart.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Failover strategy** – Decides how much of the running job graph must be restarted when a task fails, distinct from the restart strategy that decides how often.
- **Region failover** – Restarts only the failed pipelined region and regions connected by the failure, leaving unrelated regions running.
- **Pipelined region** – A set of tasks connected by streaming, record-by-record data exchanges, bounded by blocking exchanges.
- **Full restart** – Cancels and restarts every task in the entire job, simple but wasteful when independent regions exist.
- **Default** – Region failover has been the default since Flink 1.9 because it limits the blast radius of a single failure.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India runs several independent processing lines in the same hall. If one clerk on one line stumbles, the full-restart approach evacuates the entire hall and restarts every line from scratch, even the lines that were working perfectly. The region-failover approach tells only the affected line to stop and restart from its last saved state, while the other independent lines keep working undisturbed.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Failover Strategy Comparison

  Full Restart:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Region 1     Region 2     Region 3     │
  │  [Source_A]   [Source_B]   [Source_C]   │
  │  [Filter_A]   [Agg_B]     [Join_C]     │
  │  [Sink_A]     [Sink_B]    [Sink_C]     │
  │                                         │
  │  Filter_A fails → ALL regions restart   │
  │  ████████████████████████████████████   │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Region Failover:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Region 1     Region 2     Region 3     │
  │  [Source_A]   [Source_B]   [Source_C]   │
  │  [Filter_A]   [Agg_B]     [Join_C]     │
  │  [Sink_A]     [Sink_B]    [Sink_C]     │
  │                                         │
  │  Filter_A fails → only Region 1 restarts│
  │  ████████████   (running)   (running)   │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

```text
  Pipelined Region Boundaries

  Streaming job (one region):
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Source ──pipe──▶ Filter ──pipe──▶ Sink │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  Batch job (three regions):
  ┌────────┐  blocking  ┌────────┐  blocking  ┌──────┐
  │ Source  │──────────▶│  Agg   │──────────▶│ Sink  │
  │Region 1│           │Region 2│           │Region 3│
  └────────┘           └────────┘           └────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A Flink failover strategy decides how much of the running job graph has to restart when a task fails, distinct from the restart strategy that decides how often to retry. There are two failover strategies. Full restart cancels and restarts every task in the whole job, which is simple but wastes work on unrelated tasks. Region failover, the default since Flink 1.9, restarts only the failed pipelined region and any regions whose intermediate results were lost, leaving independent regions running.

The real advantage appears in jobs with multiple independent pipelines or in batch jobs with blocking exchanges. A failure in one pipeline restarts only that pipeline's region while the others keep working. In a streaming job that forms one big pipelined region, both strategies restart the same tasks, but region failover is still the correct default.

At the National Bank of India we hosted three independent pipelines in one Flink application: fraud scoring, interest calculation, and regulatory reporting. With region failover, when the interest pipeline hit a failure, only the interest region restarted while fraud detection and reporting kept running, which was critical because stopping fraud detection during an unrelated recovery would have been unacceptable.

Remember one sentence: region failover restarts only the failed pipelined region and its dependents, leaving unrelated pipelines running, which is why it is the default and more efficient than restarting the entire job.
